sentences: In a neighborhood of the city at the height of the crack epidemic, an Afro-Cuban drug dealer finds a boy, a withdrawn child who goes by a nickname, hiding from bullies in a crackhouse.
The dealer lets the boy spend the night with him and his girlfriend before returning the boy to his mother.
The boy continues to spend time with the dealer, who begins to teach him the basics of life, from which he believes the boy can benefit.
One night, the dealer encounters the mother smoking crack with one of his customers.
The dealer berates her for neglecting her son, but she rebukes him for selling crack to her in the first place.
They argue over the boy's upbringing; the mother asks if the dealer is prepared to explain to the boy why he gets tormented by his peers, alluding to him being gay.
She goes home and takes out her frustration on the boy.
The next day, the boy admits to the dealer and the girlfriend that he hates his mother and asks what a "faggot" is.
The dealer tells him it is "a word used to make gay people feel bad."
He tells the boy there is nothing wrong with being gay and that he should not allow others to mock him.
The boy then asks the dealer whether he sells drugs and whether his mother does drugs.
After the dealer remorsefully answers yes to both questions, the boy leaves as the dealer hangs his head in shame.
Now a teenager, the boy balances avoiding a school bully and spending time with the girlfriend, who lives alone after the dealer's death.
The mother, who has turned to prostitution due to her worsening addiction, forces the boy to give her the money he receives from the girlfriend.
The boy's childhood friend tells him about a detention he received for having sex with a girl in a school stairwell.
The boy later dreams about the friend and the girl having sex in the girlfriend's backyard, waking with a start.
One night, the friend visits the boy at the beach near his house.
While smoking a blunt together, the two discuss their ambitions and the friend's nickname for the boy.
They kiss, and the friend gives the boy a handjob.
The next day, the bully manipulates the friend into participating in a hazing ritual.
The friend reluctantly punches the boy until he cannot stand, watching as the bully and other boys savagely attack him.
When the principal urges him to reveal his attackers' identities, the boy refuses, saying that reporting them will not solve anything.
The next day, the enraged boy walks into class and smashes a chair over the bully's head before being restrained.
The boy is arrested and taken from the high school in a police cruiser while the friend watches.
A year and decade later, now going by that nickname, the boy, now an adult, deals drugs in another city and is an imposing figure in his community.
He receives frequent calls from the mother, who asks him to visit her at the drug treatment center where she lives.
One morning, the friend unexpectedly calls and invites the man to see him should he ever come to the city.
The man visits the mother and stands up to her for neglecting him.
The mother apologizes for not loving her son when he needed it most and says she loves him even if he does not love her back.
The two tearfully reconcile.
The man drives to the city to visit the friend at the diner where he works as a cook.
The friend makes a meal for the man, who does not respond to questions about his life and how he has seemingly changed.
The friend shares that he had a son with an ex-girlfriend and, after getting out of prison, is fulfilled by his role as a father.
The man reveals his unexpected drug dealing, which disappoints the friend, and asks the friend why he called.
The friend plays a song on the jukebox, the song that made him think of the man.
The two go to the friend's apartment.

The friend tells the man that although his life did not turn out as he had hoped, he is happy, resulting in the man admitting that he has not been intimate with anybody since their encounter years ago.
As the friend comforts him, the man remembers himself as a child, standing on a beach in the moonlight.
The actor is a burnt out American movie star who arrives in the city to appear in lucrative advertisements for a company's whiskey.
He stays at a hotel and is miserable due to problems within his twenty-five-year marriage and a midlife crisis.
The young woman, another American staying at the hotel, is a young university graduate in philosophy who is accompanying her husband while he works as a celebrity photographer.
She is feeling similarly disenchanted as she questions her marriage and is anxious about her future.
They both struggle additionally with bouts of jet lag and culture shock in the city and pass the time loitering around the hotel, the young woman also trying ikebana by chance.
The young woman is repelled by a vacuous movie actress, who is also at the hotel promoting a film.
The actress bumps into the young woman and her husband, gushing over photography sessions she has previously done with him.
The actor and the young woman frequently cross paths in the hotel and eventually start to connect in the hotel bar.
After several encounters, when her husband is on assignment outside the city, the young woman invites the actor into the city to meet some local friends.
They bond over an evening in the city, where they experience the city nightlife together and end up singing at a karaoke box.
In the days that follow, the actor and the young woman spend more time together, and their friendship strengthens.
One night while watching television and drinking sake, while neither can sleep, the two share an intimate conversation about the young woman's personal uncertainties and their married lives.
The actor has a cold conversation with his wife, then spends the night with a jazz singer from the hotel bar.
The young woman hears the woman singing in the actor's room the next morning, leading to tension between the actor and the young woman during a shabu-shabu lunch together.
The pair encounter each other in the evening and the actor reveals that he will be leaving the city the following day.
The actor and the young woman reconcile and express how they will miss each other, making a final visit to the hotel bar.
The next morning, when the actor is leaving the hotel, he and the young woman share sincere but unsatisfactory goodbyes.
On the actor's taxi ride to the airport, he sees the young woman on a crowded street, stops the car, and walks to her.
He then embraces her and whispers something in her ear.
The two share a kiss and say goodbye before the actor departs.
Following his usage in a "guess the weight" contest at an agricultural show, an orphaned piglet is brought home to the farm of the contest winner.

There, he is taken in by a Border Collie, her irascible husband and their puppies and befriends a duck, who wakes people by crowing like a rooster every morning so he will be considered useful and be spared from being eaten.
Dismayed when the farmer's family buy an alarm clock, the duck persuades the piglet to help him get rid of it.
In doing so, they wake the family's cat and wreck the house in the ensuing chaos.
The male dog sternly instructs the piglet to stay away from the duck and the house.
Seeing the collie saddened when her puppies are put up for sale, the piglet lets her adopt him.

With the family's relatives visiting for Christmas, the farmer decides against choosing the piglet for Christmas dinner and tells his wife that the piglet may bring a prize for ham at the next agricultural show.
The duck's love interest is served instead, prompting the duck to escape the farm.
The piglet investigates the fields, where he witnesses a pair of sheep rustlers stealing the farmer's sheep and quickly alerts the collie and the farmer, preventing the rustlers from taking them all.
Impressed after seeing the piglet sort hens, separating the brown from the white ones, the farmer takes him to try and herd the sheep.
Encouraged by an elderly sheep, the piglet gets the sheep to cooperate by asking nicely, but the male dog perceives the piglet's actions as an insult to sheepdogs.
When the collie stands up for the piglet, the male dog attacks and injures her and bites the farmer's hand when he tries to intervene.
The male dog is subsequently chained to the dog house and sedated, leaving the sheep herding job to the piglet.
One morning, the piglet scares off a trio of feral dogs attacking the sheep, but the elderly sheep is mortally injured and dies as a result.

The farmer, thinking the piglet was responsible, attempts to shoot him dead, but the collie finds out the truth from the other sheep and distracts the farmer long enough for his wife to inform him about the dogs' attack on a neighbouring farm.
When the farmer's wife leaves on a trip, the farmer signs the piglet up for sheepdog trials.
As it is raining the night before, the farmer lets him and the collie into the house, where he is scratched by the cat, who in turn is temporarily confined outside as punishment.
When she is let back in later, she gets back at the piglet by revealing that humans consume pigs.
After learning from the collie that this is true, the piglet runs away and the male dog finds him the next morning in a cemetery.
The farmer brings the demoralised piglet home, where he refuses to eat.
After the farmer sings a song and dances a jig for him, the piglet's faith in his affection is restored.
At the trials, the piglet meets the sheep that he will be herding, but they ignore his attempts to speak to them.
As the farmer is criticised by the bewildered judges and ridiculed by the public for not using a dog, the male dog runs back to the farm to ask the sheep what to do.
After he promises that he will treat them better from now on, the sheep disclose to him a secret password.
He returns in time to convey the password to the piglet and the sheep now follow his instructions flawlessly.
Amid the crowd's acclamation, the piglet is unanimously given a perfect score.
When the piglet sits down next to the farmer, the latter praises him with the standard command to sheep dogs that their job is done, "That'll do, Pig.
In the frame story, a grandfather reads a novel to his sick grandson, who reluctantly listens.
The heroine is a young woman living on a farm in the kingdom.
Her farmhand obediently follows her stringent commands, always responding with "As you wish."
The heroine eventually realizes the farmhand is saying he loves her, and she reciprocates his feelings.
The farmhand leaves to seek his fortune overseas so they can marry, but his ship is attacked by a pirate, who infamously leaves no survivors.
Five years later, the heroine, still grief-stricken, is forcibly betrothed to the kingdom's arrogant prince.
Before the wedding, she is kidnapped by a crafty Sicilian criminal and his accomplices: a gentle giant, and an expert Spanish swordsman, who seeks a six-fingered man that killed his father.
A masked man in black pursues them across the sea, as do the prince and his soldiers.
Atop the cliffs, the man in black defeats the swordsman in a sword duel and knocks him out, chokes the giant into unconsciousness, and kills the criminal by tricking him into drinking poison.
He absconds with the heroine ahead of the prince's party.
When the heroine identifies him as the pirate, she rebukes him for killing the farmhand and shoves him into a ravine.
While tumbling down, he shouts, "As you wish!"
Realizing he is the farmhand, the heroine tumbles after him and they reunite.
The couple then flees into the dangerous swamp to avoid the prince's party.
In the swamp, the farmhand explains that the pirate's name is an inherited title.
The previous pirate spared and recruited the farmhand, then retired and passed the mantle on to him.
Having found the heroine, the farmhand intends to do the same.
The prince captures the couple at the swamp's exit, but the heroine agrees to return with the prince after he promises to release the farmhand.
The prince then secretly orders his advisor the count, the six-fingered man, to take the farmhand to his torture chamber, the pit.
After a nightmare, the heroine threatens to kill herself if the prince marries her.

He placates her by promising to find the farmhand, then privately confides in the count that he plans to murder the heroine, which the criminal failed to do, and subsequently declare war on the neighboring country.
To maintain the ruse, the prince has his enforcers organize a "brute squad" to clear out the nearby thieves' forest.
The giant, as part of the brute squad, finds the swordsman drunk in the forest, sobers him up, and informs him of the count's existence.
Recalling the farmhand's versatility and intelligence, the swordsman and the giant search for him to help them kill the count.
The heroine discovers the prince's duplicity and labels him a coward.
Enraged, he imprisons her and tortures the farmhand seemingly to death.
The swordsman and the giant follow the farmhand's screams to the pit, discover his lifeless body, and take it to a folk healer whom the prince recently fired.
The healer declares that the farmhand is only "mostly dead", and after the swordsman promises that the farmhand can humiliate the prince, the healer and his wife concoct a pill to revive him.
The giant and the swordsman revive the farmhand with the pill, rendering him conscious but barely able to move.
By impersonating the pirate, the three infiltrate the castle as the wedding begins and encounter the count, who flees with the swordsman in pursuit.
Despite an ambush from the count, the swordsman kills him.
At the wedding, the prince impatiently rushes the ceremony, then sends the heroine to her chambers.
Before she can commit suicide, the farmhand intercepts the heroine and reminds her that she never gave her vows, invalidating the marriage.
The prince discovers them and challenges the farmhand to a duel, but the farmhand intimidates the prince into submission.
The swordsman reunites with the couple, and the farmhand offers him the pirate's title.
The three escape on horseback with the giant, and as dawn breaks, the farmhand and the heroine share a passionate kiss.
The sick grandson eagerly asks his grandfather to read him the story again the next day.
His grandfather replies, "As you wish."
